turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - cdft_piezo_d_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `d_ij` (the
    piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij|, in pC/N).
  - cdft_piezo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose
    properties are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the LARGEST
piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij| (in pC/N), then select the 5 best
candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The largest piezoelectric responses in the training set arise from two well-defined families: (i) cubic non-centrosymmetric sulvanite/anti-sulvanite structures (Na3SbS4 149 pC/N, TaTl3S4 132 pC/N) and (ii) polar, lone-pair-distorted halide perovskites (RbPbBr3 154 pC/N).  

K3SbS4 (c043) is isostructural with Na3SbS4 (identical Wyckoff positions, only Na\to K substitution) and is therefore expected to retain a giant max|d_ij|.  
The three Ge(II) chlorides (c025 InGeCl3, c026 InGeCl3, c041 KGeCl3) adopt the same distorted-perovskite topology as RbPbBr3, with stereochemically active Ge 4s2 lone pairs providing the polar distortion; they are consequently predicted to lie in the same 100 pC/N regime.  

A fifth high-response candidate is SiS2 (c036). Its edge-sharing tetrahedral chain structure is identical to those of GeS2 (38 pC/N) and TiS2 (104 pC/N), placing it well above the remaining pool entries (wurtzites, chalcopyrites, half-Heuslers, etc.), whose training analogues never exceed ~60 pC/N.  

Thus the ranking by expected max|d_ij| is c043 > c025 > c041 > c026 > c036.

Final: c043, c025, c041, c026, c036
